pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, active comparator-controlled (vs. aflibercept 2 mg Q8W), parallel-group
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in BCVA averaged over Weeks 40, 44, and 48 (non-inferiority margin 4 letters)
pivotal_trials.result: Faricimab +5.8 letters vs. aflibercept +5.1 letters; difference 0.7 (95% CI: -1.1, 2.5); non-inferiority demonstrated (lower CI bound -1.1 > -4)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-masked, active comparator-controlled (vs. aflibercept 2 mg Q8W), three parallel groups (faricimab Q8W, faricimab PTI, aflibercept Q8W)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in BCVA averaged over Weeks 48, 52, and 56 (non-inferiority margin 4 letters); key secondary: proportion with ≥2-step DR severity improvement at Week 52
pivotal_trials.result: Faricimab Q8W +10.7 letters, faricimab PTI +11.6 letters vs. aflibercept +10.9 letters; differences: Q8W -0.2 (97.5% CI: -2.0, 1.6), PTI +0.7 (97.5% CI: -1.1, 2.5); non-inferiority demonstrated for both arms; superiority not demonstrated

key_safety: The most common ocular adverse events with faricimab were conjunctival hemorrhage (~8%) and cataract (~12% in DME studies), with intraocular inflammation rates of ~3% (nAMD) and ~1.4–1.7% (DME), all broadly comparable to aflibercept; a post-marketing study of corneal endothelial health was required.
target_moa: Dual inhibition of VEGF-A and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) via bispecific humanized CrossMAb antibody

_meta.indication:
VABYSMO is a vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and angiopoietin 2 (Ang-2) inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with:
- Neovascular (wet) Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD)
- Diabetic Macular Edema (DME)

supplements.description: Updated prescribing information for Vabysmo (farcimab-svoa) to include second-year clinical data from the YOSEMITE and RHINE studies in "patients with diabetic macular edema"; no new indication, population, dose, or route of administration was added.

Expanded indication to include **the treatment of macular edema following retinal vein occlusion (RVO)** for Vabysmo (faricimab-svoa), a condition for which pediatric studies were waived as it does not occur in the pediatric population.

Removed the 6-month duration limit for monthly dosing of Vabysmo (faricimab-svoa) in the treatment of macular edema following retinal vein occlusion (RVO), allowing monthly dosing beyond the previously specified 6-month cap.
